newsitem.title: CHINA: China state bank income tax cut to 33 pct from Jan.
newsitem.headline: China state bank income tax cut to 33 pct from Jan.

text.p: Income tax levied on state-owned banks and insurance enterprises have been cut to 33 percent from 55 percent from January 1, Minister of Finance Liu Zhongli said in his annual budget speech on Sunday.
This brings the rate into line with that levied on other Chinese-funded firms, Liu told the annual session of the National People's Congress, or parliament.
The business tax rate for all banks and insurance companies had been increased to eight percent from five percent, he said.
The changes had been made to enable a balance revenue distribution between the government and enterprises and between central and local authorities, Liu said.
It was also intended to enhance the central government's macro-economic control, he said but did not elaborate.

The percentage of revenue from stamp duty on securities transactions had also been readjusted, with 80 percent of income now going to the central government and the remainder to local authorities, Liu said but gave no further details.
